text:
violet: quick triage thread for rv7 bring-up in staging. overall NDCG@10 +1.6% but weird MRR@5 drop on ultra-short queries (<=3 tokens) -4.6%. pasting slice table and hypotheses.

harry: can you paste the slices? curious if it's locale/code/anchors.

violet: table from run-zip-701:
```
metric        overall   ultra_short (<=3)   short (4-6)   others
NDCG@10       +1.6%     +0.4%               +1.8%          +2.1%
MRR@5         -0.2%     -4.6%               -0.9%          +0.6%
Top1_rate     -0.6pp   -6.9pp              -2.1pp         +0.3pp
```
change log: rv7 includes query-prefix-priming (append "Q: <query>\nA:" to candidate surfaces), anchor-aware dedupe (merge candidates with fuzzy overlap), and int8 PTQ with symmetric rounding.

sophia: interesting pattern: NDCG improves, top1 down -> probability mass shifted to more items. prefix-priming can boost synonyms across long docs but may hurt exact anchors used by very short queries.

harry: also check candidate merging: fuzzy dedupe may be collapsing near-duplicates such that the highest-precision candidate is merged with a lower-precision one and loses its standout score. That would kill top1.

violet: good idea. queued ablation matrix: (A) disable prefix-priming, (B) disable fuzzy-dedupe, (C) both off, (D) same but quant=fp16. eval command: 
```
./eval_rerank --model rv7 --dataset holdout_v7 \
  --prefix_priming {on,off} --fuzzy_dedupe {on,off} --quant {int8,fp16}
```
ETA ~14m.

eval-bot: Job 701 queued by violet. ETA ~14m.

harry: also collect top1_prob_mass, merged_candidate_count, and exact_anchor_match_rate. Those will help.

eval-bot: Job 701 completed. quick deltas vs baseline (new rv7 config):
- A (prefix_priming=off, fuzzy_dedupe=on, quant=int8): ultra_short MRR delta = +2.9% (partial recovery)
- B (prefix_priming=on, fuzzy_dedupe=off, quant=int8): ultra_short MRR delta = +3.3% (partial recovery)
- C (both off, quant=int8): ultra_short MRR delta = +6.0% (full recovery beyond baseline)
- D (both off, quant=fp16): ultra_short MRR delta = +6.8% (slightly better)
Additional stats: merged_candidate_count decreased by 42% in B (fuzzy off), exact_anchor_match_rate increased by 5.6pp in C, top1_prob_mass recovered by ~6.9pp in C.

sophia: so both prefix priming and fuzzy dedupe contribute; together they caused candidate dilution for ultra-short queries. Quantization (int8) subtracts ~0.7pp on top1 for this slice.

harry: prefix priming probably spreads tokens from query into all candidates so short exact matches lose their discriminative signal. fuzzy dedupe merging can combine a precise snippet with a noisy longer doc and reduce peak.

violet: actionables: 1) revert prefix_priming for queries <=3 tokens (keep for long queries), 2) tune fuzzy_dedupe to preserve exact-anchor-first preference (if candidate contains exact anchor substring, prefer it when merging), 3) schedule a tiny per-slice PTQ calibration for ultra-short sensitive layers.

sophia: agree. Also add a unit test in the rerank eval harness: synthetic few-token queries that expect top1_prob_mass > X and ensure any change that drops >1.5pp fails CI.

harry: any objections to a quick 5% A/B with the prefix_priming exception only? That will be fastest.

violet: starting rollout: https://go/rollout/rv7-ultrashort-prefix-exception (5% 2h -> 25% 4h -> 100%). deploying now. ops-bot will schedule.

ops-bot: Rollout created by violet: rv7-ultrashort-prefix-exception. Target 5% for 2h. Safety flag: hold Dedicated rollout until A/B green.

eval-bot: A/B arm collecting online top1/mrr/exact_match every 5m.

sophia: small note: prefix_priming did help long docs in offline evals; we want to keep it for most traffic. so this exception is low-risk and reversible.

harry: follow-up ticket: implement anchor-preserve merge logic in fuzzy_dedupe and add a configuration knob to set anchor_priority_threshold. assigning to infra/metrics + rerank infra.

violet: filing tickets and tests now. will post prod A/B numbers here. thanks for the quick triage. :white_check_mark:
